events.title: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama
events.description: Publius Cornelius Scipio defeated Hannibal near Zama in North Africa; 19 October is the traditional date. The victory ended the Second Punic War, leaving Rome dominant in the western Mediterranean.
events.html: Publius Cornelius Scipio defeated Hannibal near Zama in North Africa; 19 October is the traditional date. The victory ended the Second Punic War, leaving Rome dominant in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: King John dies at Newark Castle
events.description: King John died of dysentery at Newark during a civil war with his barons and a French invasion. His nine-year-old son became Henry III, and his regents reissued Magna Carta to win back support.
events.html: King John died of dysentery at Newark during a civil war with his barons and a French invasion. His nine-year-old son became Henry III, and his regents reissued Magna Carta to win back support.

events.title: Heidelberg University holds its first lecture
events.description: A day after a Pontifical High Mass established it, Heidelberg University, founded by Rupert I, Elector Palatine, held its first lecture, making it the oldest university in present-day Germany. By March 1390 it had 185 students.
events.html: A day after a Pontifical High Mass established it, Heidelberg University, founded by Rupert I, Elector Palatine, held its first lecture, making it the oldest university in present-day Germany. By March 1390 it had 185 students.

events.title: Bordeaux falls to the French, ending the Hundred Years' War
events.description: Three months after the English defeat at Castillon, Bordeaux surrendered to the French, ending three centuries of English rule in Gascony. No more hostilities followed, and the Hundred Years' War was over.
events.html: Three months after the English defeat at Castillon, Bordeaux surrendered to the French, ending three centuries of English rule in Gascony. No more hostilities followed, and the Hundred Years' War was over.

events.title: The Second Peace of Thorn ends the Thirteen Years' War
events.description: The Polish king Casimir IV Jagiellon and the Teutonic Knights made peace at Toruń, ending the longest of the Polish–Teutonic Wars. Royal Prussia, with Danzig and Marienburg, passed to Poland; the Order kept the rest as a Polish fief.
events.html: The Polish king Casimir IV Jagiellon and the Teutonic Knights made peace at Toruń, ending the longest of the Polish–Teutonic Wars. Royal Prussia, with Danzig and Marienburg, passed to Poland; the Order kept the rest as a Polish fief.

events.title: Cornwallis's army surrenders at Yorktown
events.description: Besieged by American and French forces, Lord Cornwallis's army of about 8,000 surrendered at Yorktown, Virginia. The defeat effectively ended major fighting in the American Revolutionary War.
events.html: Besieged by American and French forces, Lord Cornwallis's army of about 8,000 surrendered at Yorktown, Virginia. The defeat effectively ended major fighting in the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Napoleon retreats after defeat at Leipzig
events.description: The Battle of the Nations ended with Napoleon's army in retreat from Leipzig, its rearguard trapped when a bridge was blown too early. He lost control of Germany, and the Allies invaded France within months.
events.html: The Battle of the Nations ended with Napoleon's army in retreat from Leipzig, its rearguard trapped when a bridge was blown too early. He lost control of Germany, and the Allies invaded France within months.

events.title: Black Monday: stock markets crash worldwide
events.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 508 points, or 22.6 per cent, its largest one-day percentage fall. Markets crashed worldwide, though the wider economy recovered far faster than after 1929.
